verdict_summary: All three primary PII failure categories from the prior audit have been resolved. Zero personal-name sole-proprietors remain in legal_business_name. poc_phone column is confirmed absent. poc_email is 100% empty (not populated). The compound PII packages (personal name + home address + personal phone) that triggered the original FAIL have been fully broken at every point. Residual: 6 LLC/Corp entities with residentially-styled addresses (no suite/floor indicator) remain in the dataset (0.13% of rows), but these do not constitute compound PII — no personal name or phone is attached to any of them, all are proper legal business entities under FFATA mandatory public disclosure, and the source_url on every row directs users to the authoritative SAM.gov entity page rather than personal contact information. Dataset is cleared for distribution under standard B2B disclosure conditions.

remediation_effectiveness.note_on_count_discrepancy: Original audit estimated 7,541 rows; actual parsed CSV (handling embedded newlines in quoted fields) was 4,869 rows pre-remediation. After stripping 138 rows, output is 4,731. The original audit's row estimates were based on raw line count, not parsed CSV records — this explains the variance between estimated removals (253 personal-name, 2,120 residential) and actual removals (19 personal-name, 119 residential).

check_a_personal_name_sole_proprietors.method: Regex scan of all 4,731 legal_business_name values. Pattern: LASTNAME, FIRSTNAME (2+ character tokens, comma separator) with no entity-type suffix keyword. Two-pass with apostrophe-name and trailing-initial variants. Also checked for DBA personal-name patterns.

residual_residential_risk.risk_assessment: LOW — materially different from original FAIL conditions. (1) All 6 are proper legal business entities (Inc, LLC, Corp, P.C.) — not natural persons registered under personal names. (2) No poc_phone attached to any row. (3) No poc_email attached to any row. (4) All have SAM.gov source_url providing verifiable public entity page. (5) All are FFATA-mandated public disclosures. The compound PII package (personal name + home address + personal phone) that triggered the original FAIL is broken at every point for these residual entries. Risk is limited to: a business entity's registered address that may coincide with the owner's home — without any personal contact information, this is commercially standard (Dun & Bradstreet, ReferenceUSA, and similar databases retain home-based business registrations).
residual_residential_risk.compliance_ruling: Does not independently trigger Rule 2 FAIL given absence of compound identifiers. Noted as residual and disclosed in shipping conditions.

check_c_poc_phone_absent.finding: poc_phone column confirmed not present in dataset schema. Validation check poc_phone_absent also returned PASS. Column was dropped during remediation Step 3.

check_d_poc_email_clean.finding: All 4,731 rows have poc_email = '' (empty string, equivalent to N/A/not populated). Zero rows contain any email address. Data engineer correctly withheld this field as it requires SAM.gov entity API (registered API key) — consistent with public-data-only Rule 1 compliance.

rules_applied: Rule 1: Public data only — no auth-bypass, no scraping behind login, no purchased private datasets
Rule 2: No PII — personal email, phone, home address, financial accounts → automatic FAIL
Rule 3: Source URL on every row
Rule 4: Production code only (dataset integrity — no mocks, placeholders, or half-built data)

rule_1_public_data.notes: Carried forward from prior audit — source is USASpending.gov /api/v2/download/awards/, federally mandated public transparency API (FFATA). No auth bypass, no login scraping, no purchased data. Remediation did not alter sourcing. poc_email correctly withheld (SAM.gov entity API requires registered key — data engineer defaulted to empty, preserving Rule 1 compliance).
